newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty stable vs basket in moribund trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty stable vs basket in moribund trade.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed the trendless session virtually flat against the currency basket amid thin trade in the absence of larger buy or sell orders, dealers said.
They said trade was light also because the range-bound dollar/mark European trade failed to give the Polish currency any impulse to move.

"Nothing happened on the domestic market, and the zloty was additionally anchored against the trading band centre by the motionless European dollar/mark ahead of the holiday in U.S.," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki from ING Bank in Warsaw
The zloty closed at 1.98/1.96 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's 2.02/1.97 percent from parity rate.
It was at 2.8152/59 to the dollar, down from 2.8140/50 on Friday and at 1.8390/96 to the mark, flat from 1.8385/00.

Short term interbank deposit market traded stable below 19 percent, and was not much influenced by the central banks' moderate intervention. NBP drained 364 million zlotys for 14-days at an unchanged maximum rate of 19.14 percent.
Overnight deposits closed at 18.00/18.40 percent versus opening's 18.00/18.7 percent, tomorrow/next deposits closed at 18.25/18.45 percent against 17.80/18.50 percent at opening.
Minimum prices of most Polish T-bills fell at today's primary auction on demand matching the 1.2 billion zloty offer, but average yields remained unchanged.

The average yield of the benchmark 52-week paper was flat at 19.43 percent. The yield rose by 0.02 to 19.11 percent for the 26-week paper and was unchanged for the 13- and 8-week bills at 18.55 and 18.11 percent respectively.
